programme.title: Origins: The Tigers Swoop
programme.desc: The USS President Garfield was heading to China. His true task was to assess the condition of China's air force. His planned three month assignment turned into eight years of warfare. By its end, he would be a major general and the unity created, the Flying Tigers, would be the most famous squadron in the history of aerial warfare.

programme.title: 1942 - The Dieppe Raid
programme.desc: Dieppe 1942, the mention of this name and date is enough to recall the sinister memory of an allied raid composed essentially of Canadian troops. On August 19, after 9 hours of fighting, 1,197 Allied soldiers, including 913 Canadians, were killed. 48 French civilians also died... At the height of the fighting, the attackers lost four men per second. The Dieppe raid turned into a massacre!

programme.title: Blitzkrieg
programme.desc: Six months have passed with very little action in the Phony War. That is about to end and a new word is added to the vocabulary of warfare - Blitzkrieg.

programme.title: Episode 4
programme.desc: In a war-torn setting, a group of pilots and their loved ones grapple with personal struggles and relationships. Secrets are revealed, hearts are broken, and friendships are tested amidst the chaos of war. As they face danger and uncertainty, they must find strength and solace in each other to navigate through their challenging circumstances.

programme.title: Action T4: A Doctor Under Nazism
programme.desc: This documentary recounts his story and through the man's story, that of the so-called 'Action T4'. Action T4 consisted of eliminating physical and mental disabilities and those people considered by the Nazi regime to be useless or 'asocial'.

programme.title: Hitler's Desert War
programme.desc: While the British army puts the Italian forces to rout, Hitler sends the Afrika Korps led by the general Rommel for help. The Desert fox keeps on winning battles until Montgomery, the British commander, sets up a plan to crush his opponent. After the American landing in North Africa the Axis armies have no choice but to surrender and put an end to the Desert War on May the 13rd of 1943.

programme.title: Rolling Power
programme.desc: The basic combat formation of the modern land army is the division. Divisions contain all of the elements needed to wage land combat including infantry, armor, artillery and other supporting arms. Divisions are substantial in size from 10,000 to 20,000 troops, nearly 500 armored vehicles and 2000 other vehicles.

programme.title: The Blitz the Bismarck and Barbarossa: April-June 1941
programme.desc: With Britain failing to fall, the Blitz drew to a close, the sinking of the German battleship, the Bismarck, lifted the spirits of the British Navy. Hitler's campaign for Russia, Operation Barbarossa, got underway, the course of World War II changed.

programme.title: Russian Roulette: July-September 1941
programme.desc: Hitler had expected a decisive victory in Russia, he was thwarted at every turn and while the Luftwaffe bombed Moscow and the Siege of Leningrad began, the Soviet Red Army refused to capitulate. They just watched and waited for the winter snows.

programme.title: Establishing the Beachhead
programme.desc: Landing Craft - Establishing Beachead. Silent film.

programme.title: Keeping the Railways Open
programme.desc: French civilians and U.S. Army engineers repair and salvage railroad yards, bridges, and trains.

programme.title: Floating Fortress
programme.desc: Mission of the battleship in Korea. Life aboard, and compartmentational operations.

programme.title: Episode 2
programme.desc: Sir David reveals true stories of unbelievable heroism in World War II, in a world of cold-blooded assassins, crack saboteurs, elite commandos, playboy spies, super-villains and femmes fatales.

programme.title: Carey Mulligan
programme.desc: Carey Mulligan's grandfather Denzil Booth, travelled thousands of miles to fight the Japanese in the final months of the war. His university education meant Denzil was fast-tracked to be a junior officer in the Navy. He lost his closest friends on board the first ever ship to be attacked by a Japanese Kamikaze. Carey travels to Japan to understand the culture of the Kamikaze from the other side.

programme.title: Overlord
programme.desc: In 1943, the Axis was on the defensive everywhere. In 1944, The Allies strength would grow in the East, and in the Soviet Union with the opening of the second front.

programme.title: Medal of Honor Winners
programme.desc: True stories of the Medal of Honor, the highest award for valor which can be bestowed upon an individual serving in the Armed Services of the United States.

programme.title: German Jets and Destroyers
programme.desc: Three years after the end of WW1, civil aviation was permitted in Germany and names that were later to spearhead military aircraft production emerged. Names such as Messerschmittt, Heinkel and Yunkers. This documentary discusses the rise of the top German Jets and Destroyers used in battle during WW2.

programme.title: Rough Riders
programme.desc: Speeding behind German lines the men of Troop A, in their armored cars and half-tracks left destruction and fear in their wake. Surprising the German garrison at the town of Epernay, they established an outpost from which they could defend a counter-attack. Outnumbered and outgunned with thirteen rounds of ammunition left, these brave GI's held this vital town until re-enforcements could arrive.

programme.title: Episode 12
programme.desc: Amidst WWII's war-torn skies, Soviet Major Bestuzhev defends the airdrome. A bond forms with comrade Zhenya, but facing overwhelming odds, they must protect their homeland, confronting fears in a narrative of sacrifice, courage, and camaraderie. As the air raid sirens wail, they delve deeper into the turmoil of war, discovering the true essence of duty and the resilience of the human spirit.

programme.title: A Century of Tanks
programme.desc: April 16, 1917, for the first time in history, French tanks fight their way through the black sludge of Chemin des Dames. One year before, in October, British tanks tried their luck in Somme. In both cases, the long-awaited miracle did not take place. Yet, a century later, the tanks are still here, monsters of technology that are becoming increasingly efficient.

programme.title: The Year 1944
programme.desc: Roosevelt, Churchill, and Stalin congregate at the Teheran Conference in 1943. U.S. troops land and fight on Kwajalein, Eniwetok, Saipan, Guam, and other Pacific islands. Russian troops advance to Romania and capture German soldiers. Paratroops jump at Caen. Citizens of Rome, Paris, Bucharest, Brussels, Belgrade, and Athens celebrate their liberation. F.D.R. addresses the United Nations.

programme.title: Japan Surrenders
programme.desc: Tokyo Bay, Japan. September 2, 1945. On board the USS Missouri, an American battleship. Several weeks ago, American atom bombs devastated Hiroshima and Nagasaki. Japan has capitulated. This morning at 9, eleven Japanese government and military officials climb aboard the Missouri to sign the surrender agreement.

programme.title: NEWSREEL FOOTAGE OF THE NAZI WAR CRIMINALS
programme.desc: Nazi war criminals are put on trial for their war crimes committed during WWII. This program covers various events from the Lublin Massacre, German atrocities in concentration camps and many others

programme.title: Episode 3
programme.desc: A Soviet intelligence officer, long operating as Major Feller, flees the German rear with secret documents detailing enemy fortifications and mines. He links with partisans but they're trapped. Command merges Makeev's saboteurs with Zvonareva's unit: saboteurs seize an improvised German airfield while pilots land behind enemy lines to bring Feller to HQ.

programme.title: U-Boat Alert!
programme.desc: World War II at sea was marked by the rise of submarines, leading to fierce battles above and below the waves. Crews faced overcrowding and claustrophobia in these confined spaces. This technological evolution paved the way for modern submarines. Developed by Germany, submarines became as crucial to naval warfare as strategic bombers were to the skies, with other countries soon following suit.

programme.title: Episode 2
programme.desc: Sir David reveals true stories of unbelievable heroism in World War II, in a world of cold-blooded assassins, crack saboteurs, elite commandos, playboy spies, super-villains and femmes fatales.

programme.title: Pilots at War
programme.desc: Watch as a B-17 Flying Fortress and its crew fights its way over Nazi occupied Europe, battling the enemy's ME-109s and FW-190s. Witness all the fear and excitement of air combat as fighters spit out machine gun fire and brave deadly ground fire.

programme.title: Happy New Year
programme.desc: The Germans launch a last desperate air and ground attack to coincide with the arrival of the last year of the war, and, whilst improved flying conditions enable the US air forces to bring added strength to the battle, the troops on the ground continue to suffer the effects of the coldest Belgian winter in history.

programme.title: Army Group Center
programme.desc: The Wehrmacht organized into 3 army groups for operation. North headed to Stalingrad, South, toward Ukraine, and centre towards the heartland of Russia. Led by General field marshall Fedor Von Bonk, a well known anti nazi, army group centre was the largest and best equipped of all 3 groups. It also contained Gen. Heinz Guderian, perhaps the most renowned commander of the 20th century.

programme.title: Carey Mulligan
programme.desc: Carey Mulligan's grandfather Denzil Booth, travelled thousands of miles to fight the Japanese in the final months of the war. His university education meant Denzil was fast-tracked to be a junior officer in the Navy. He lost his closest friends on board the first ever ship to be attacked by a Japanese Kamikaze. Carey travels to Japan to understand the culture of the Kamikaze from the other side.

programme.title: Overlord
programme.desc: In 1943, the Axis was on the defensive everywhere. In 1944, The Allies strength would grow in the East, and in the Soviet Union with the opening of the second front.

programme.title: Adolf and Eva
programme.desc: The protracted romance between Adolf Hitler and Eva Braun began in 1929 and ended in 1945 in the bunker under the ruins of the Chancellery. Eva was Hitler's bride for less than 40 hours before she committed suicide.

programme.title: Big Picture: Atrocities in Korea
programme.desc: A documented report of Communist atrocities in Korea, with scenes just released depicting the horror and brutality of Communism. Includes interviews with returned prisoners of war who were eye witnesses to some of these atrocities and Major General William Dean and General Mark W. Clark.

programme.title: Duel in the Desert
programme.desc: In the Iraq War, flying in the desert poses unique difficulties - the dust storm that accompanies every landing and take-off - and the lack of places to hide. When a young Royal Navy pilot comes under fire from a tank, he soon finds himself engaged in a deadly game of cat and mouse.

programme.title: Why We Fight
programme.desc: As Hitler's ambitions spread beyond Germany, the world drew toward another great war - to be fought on many battlefields, and for the hearts and minds of the people.

programme.title: America at War: October-December: 1941
programme.desc: As Hitler focussed on Russia, the situation in the Pacific developed to epic proportions when the Japanese air force attacked the American Naval Fleet at Pearl Harbour on the 7th of December. This immediately brought the USA into the Theatre of War.

programme.title: The Fall of Singapore: January-March 1942
programme.desc: With Britain no longer facing Hitler alone, the first GIs arrived in the UK. As Singapore fell, the Allies looked on in horror as Japan also had control of Java, Burma and New Guinea, as they edged ever closer towards Australia.

programme.title: The Battle of Normandy
programme.desc: The Allied landings on D Day and the subsequent battles for control of Normandy.

programme.title: The SS: A Barbaric State
programme.desc: Among the defendants are the Führer's closest surviving accomplices. But not only them: defendant number 27 is not even a man. It is an entire organization: the SS were a state within the state - which ruled all the police - with its own army, within the Nazi regime.

programme.title: Episode Three
programme.desc: This 3-part program concludes with the liberation of the concentration caps and the arrests and trials of the surviving Nazi leaders for war crimes. The end of the Second World War.

programme.title: The Ultimate History of the Messerschmitt
programme.desc: In this program we look at the development of the Bf 109 which flew in all theaters of conflict in which the Luftwaffe was involved. More Bf 109s were built than any other fighter of the era. After the war the Spanish Air Force continued to operate them but powered by the engine of its great wartime adversary the Spitfire's Rolls Royce Merlin. Also featured are the ME 262, Bf110, and ME 169 Komet.

programme.title: Decisive Battles of Hitler's War: The Fall of France
programme.desc: When Hitler claimed restitution of Sudetenland, France and Britain abandoned their ally. Ignoring offers to help defend the Czechs, French leaders met with Hitler in Munich in Sep. 1938. Hitler performed like a statesmen, and French leaders signed a treaty that was in fact a death warrant for their own countries. Hitler felt that the floodgates were open and the wave became unstoppable.

programme.title: The Battle of Berlin: The Russians Are Coming
programme.desc: The advance of the Red Army towards Berlin in the final months of WWII.

programme.title: The Allies Forge On
programme.desc: 'Independence Day in Europe - In France, Eisenhower observes General Bradley fire a giant howitzer signaling our artillery into a massed crescendo of fire. Following the landing battles in Normandy, the Canadians return to the thick of the fighting at Cariquet. So severe that some Canadian camera crew were killed. In their sector, the Yanks are blazing through the hedge rows with grenade guns.

programme.title: Episode 11
programme.desc: Amidst enemy forces gathering, a Luftwaffe squadron guards above, raising suspicions of troop relocation. A pilot's sacrifice, underwater tanks, and strategists' debates add to tensions. The mission is to destroy the enemy crossing without battles. Pilots reflect on their future amid potential encirclement and lack of aviation devices.

programme.title: Big Picture: Korean Wind Up 1953
programme.desc: The end of the Korean War and a review of the United Nations that fought against the North.

programme.title: Triumphant on Land
programme.desc: Speed and strategy have always defined warfare. This episode explores the evolution of battlefield mobility-from chariots and cavalry to Humvees and tanks. Highlighting the most iconic and influential combat vehicles, including WWII's infamous tanks, we reveal how movement has been a decisive force in shaping tactics, winning battles, and revolutionizing modern war logistics.

programme.title: Episode 2
programme.desc: Winter 1914. The first world conflict is becoming bogged down in the trenches. From now on, the war will no longer be solely on the ground. It will also be in the air. But the beginnings are difficult.

programme.title: Reinhard Heydrich
programme.desc: His fleet of U-boats killed thousands and sunk millions of tons of ships and supplies. His career spanned the depths of the ocean to the leader of a nation. At Nuremberg he was charged with piracy and murder as a Nazi War Criminal, and yet escaped the hangman. His story is now told, by both the historians and by the personal statements of those who served with him.

programme.title: Episode 1

programme.title: Time Of The Stranger

programme.title: Vengeance
programme.desc: Two men are determined to avenge their brother's death after he is killed by Lieutenant Skinner.

programme.desc: An ex-prizefighter tries to blackmail his old boss, a mafia kingpin in Detroit.

programme.title: Epitaph For A Lady

programme.title: Triangle
programme.desc: A mild-mannered Sparta businessman shoots his wife and her lover and then flees with his daughter.

programme.title: Hello In There
programme.desc: A friend of Bubba's is framed for theft and kills himself. Only his young son knows the truth.

programme.title: December Days
programme.desc: An elderly resident of a nursing home informs Chief Gillespie that a murder has taken place at the home.

programme.title: A Loss Of Innocence
programme.desc: When Jamison picks up students for cutting school, a simple truancy bust turns into a complicated murder case.

programme.title: Bubb's Baby
programme.desc: Someone mysteriously leaves a baby on Lieutenant Bubba Skinner's doorstep.

programme.title: Home Is Where The Heart Is
programme.desc: A conservative minister is murdered while trying to close down a traveling bordello operating near his church.

programme.title: An Angry Woman
programme.desc: After an employee of the high school is run off the road by the driver of a semi-truck, resulting in death.

programme.title: Indiscretions
programme.desc: After her involvement in a crime committed in Philadelphia, Regina, an old friend of Althea's runs to Sparta.

programme.title: Night Of The Killing
programme.desc: Tibbs is convinced that the right man is in custody for the murder of a cab driver, but Gillespie has doubts.

programme.title: Citizen Trundel (Part 1)

programme.title: Citizen Trundel (Part 2)
programme.desc: Harriet is determined to bring her sister's killer to justice and decides to try handling things on her own.

programme.title: Brotherly Love (Part 1)
programme.desc: When an old friend apparently commits suicide, Virgil travels to Philadelphia and uncovers corruption.

programme.desc: Gillespie travels to Philadelphia to help Tibbs, who was mistakenly arrested for the murder of a policeman

programme.desc: Gillespie and Tibbs investigate an allegation that a popular school teacher has molested a student.

programme.title: Quick Fix
programme.desc: While fishing on his day off, Bubba Skinner's dog unearths a dead baby.

programme.title: Homecoming
programme.desc: Having served his time, Prosper Hoag is on parole and back home in Sparta. Will the folks in town forgive him?

programme.desc: Gillespie's relationship with Harriet DeLong is tested when her ex-husband is caught committing a robbery.

programme.desc: Gillespie and Tibbs question the suspicious circumstances around the death of an elderly shop owner.

programme.title: Laid To Waste

programme.desc: A young witness is reluctant to come forward after a double murder at a local roadhouse.

programme.desc: An old flame of Gillespie's reappears in Sparta with her daughter, the product of the affair that they had.

programme.desc: A teacher in Sparta with her multiple romances attracts negative attention from the townsfolk.

programme.title: The More Things Change
programme.desc: Money and a secret love affair drive a businessman to stop at nothing to bring his partner down.

programme.title: Sparta Gold
programme.desc: For Bubba Skinner and his date, a picnic ends in gunshots and the discovery of a large marijuana operation.

programme.title: Tales Of Terror
programme.desc: Three short stories based on the works of Edgar Allan Poe, with Vincent Price in the starring roles and directed by the great Roger Corman.

programme.title: The Raven
programme.desc: Scream legends Vincent Price, Peter Lorre and Boris Karloff are three rival sorcerers whose paths cross when one is turned into a raven by another!

programme.title: The Haunted Palace
programme.desc: A century after a warlock was burned alive, his descendant (Vincent Price) inherits the family estate and the horrors of the past return to haunt him.

programme.title: The Masque Of The Red Death (1964)
programme.desc: Death and debauchery reign in the castle of Price Prospero (Vincent Price)...and when it reigns it pours...in this lavish Edgar Allan Poe adaptation.

programme.title: The Tomb Of Ligeia
programme.desc: Vincent Price's deceased first wife, Ligeia, casts a long shadow over his ill-advised second marriage, especially when Ligeia's spirit returns.

programme.title: Murders In The Rue Morgue
programme.desc: In Paris, a theatrical company with a specialty in Grand Guignol undertakes their most gruesome production yet! And the blood will flow!

programme.title: Necropolis
programme.desc: An evil witch is reincarnated, in modern day New York, in the form of a beautiful Vespa riding punkette. To maintain her eternally youthful status, she must sacrifice a virgin and find a sacred ring which holds tremendous powers.

programme.title: Scarecrows
programme.desc: Filled with gripping suspense and eye-popping action, this intense thriller is an unrelenting terror-fest that'll scare the stuffing out of you!

programme.title: The Black Sleep
programme.desc: Basil Rathbone, Bela Lugosi, Lon Chaney, Jr. and John Carradine star in this terrifying horror classic about a brain surgeon's unorthodox experiments.

programme.title: The Manster
programme.desc: An American reporter in Japan becomes the unwitting subject of a mad scientist's twisted experiment in this terrifying tale of ambition gone berserk.

programme.title: Count Yorga, Vampire
programme.desc: Two young lovers are stranded overnight in a van, unaware they're outside the mansion of a revenous vampire who is feeding on any trespassers!

programme.title: The Return Of Count Yorga
programme.desc: It's a love story with bite when a revived Count Yorga roams the city in search of new blood...until he finds a girl to share eternity with!

programme.title: Blacula
programme.desc: The eternally cool William Marshall puts a fresh spin on the age-old legend of the vampire, condemned to wander the Earth with an insatiable lust for blood in "Blacula," often credited as the first African American horror film.

programme.title: Scream, Blacula, Scream!
programme.desc: Brought back to the world of the living by a voodoo ceremony Blacula (William Marshall) is loosed with insatiable bloodlust upon the population of a small community in the Louisiana back country. Pam Grier also stars in this scintillating sequel

programme.title: The Amityville Horror (1979)
programme.desc: James Brolin, Margot Kidder and Rod Steiger star in this horror classic as George and Kathy Lutz (Brolin, Kidder) buy their dream home only for it to becomes a hellish nightmare as satanic forces haunt them with sheer, unbridled evil!

programme.title: Amityville 3-D
programme.desc: The home of unspeakable evil is back! Tony Roberts, Tess Harper, Robert Joy, Candy Clark and Meg Ryan star in this third outing to Amityville in which a skeptical journalist sets out to debunk the Amityville house's reputation for unspeakable evil.

programme.title: The Horror Show
programme.desc: A maniacal murderer (Brion James) returns from the depths of hell to seek revenge on the cop who captured him in this supernatural horror-fest!

programme.title: Pumpkinhead
programme.desc: In this atmospheric horror classic directed by special effect legend Stan Winston, Ed Harley (Lance Henriksen) seeks the help of a witch to invoke the demon "Pumpkinhead" in order to exact revenge on the teenagers who inadvertently killed his son.

programme.title: Monkey Shines: An Experiment In Fear
programme.desc: In this classic spine-tingler, a paralyzed man (Jason Beghe) is cared for by Ella, an intelligent monkey. But when Ella seems to begin reading Allan's darker thoughts, he must stop the cunning maniacal creature...before she takes over his mind!

programme.title: The Beast Within
programme.desc: Seventeen years after a woman is attacked by a barely glimpsed creature in a Mississippi swamp, her teenage son's beastly nature surfaces and he begins a reign of terror in this exciting story of a human-into monster transformation.

programme.title: American Gothic
programme.desc: The family that slays together stays together when six young travelers find themselves at the mercy of the eccentric Ma, Pa and their "children."

programme.title: Donovan's Brain
programme.desc: Scientist Patrick Corey has a hideous hobby - he keeps brains alive! But when the brain of dead murderer W.H. Donovan falls into his possession, he finds that it has a mind of its ownand is controlling him through telepathic messages!

programme.title: The Brain That Wouldn't Die
programme.desc: To restore the life of his fiancee, who was decapitated in an automobile accident, a brilliant surgeon tries to find a suitable body to attach to her head, which he keeps alive and locked in a dungeon. But nothing will stop her from getting revenge!

programme.title: The Monster That Challenged The World
programme.desc: The beaches go from fun-filled swim-fests to horrifying slug-fests when gargantuan vampire snails threaten to suck the life out of all mankind!

programme.title: It! The Terror From Beyond Space
programme.desc: Panic is rampant in this acclaimed thriller about a band of space explorers who suddenly find themselves being hunted by a maniacal creature.

programme.title: Killer Klowns From Outer Space
programme.desc: When a gang of alien-clowns land in a nearby area (in a ship shaped like a circus big-top), the cops are skeptical. But before long, there can be no doubt: Killer Klowns from Outer Space are here to turn the Earth's population into candy floss!

programme.title: Strange Invaders
programme.desc: Unaware the entire citizenry has been replaced by aliens, a professor arrives in a Midwestern town looking for his ex-wife who vanished.

programme.title: Invasion Of The Body Snatchers
programme.desc: Under cover of darkness, while an unsuspecting city sleeps, an alien life form begins to sow the seeds of unspeakable terror. Donald Sutherland, Brooke Adams, Leonard Nimoy, Veronica Cartwright & Jeff Goldblum star in this classic suspense thriller.

programme.title: Invaders From Mars
programme.desc: In this thrilling creature feature, a young boy's life is turned upside-down when alien invaders intent on taking over the world land in his backyard!

programme.title: The Interrogation
programme.desc: Robert Davis, who was convicted of murdering a woman and her son, claims his confession was coerced and tries to prove he is innocent.

programme.title: A Promise to Gloria
programme.desc: A mother searches for answers in the unsolved murder of her 14-year-old daughter until new DNA technology changes everything.

programme.title: The Investigation
programme.desc: A Philadelphia murder reveals decades of misconduct in the city's criminal justice system and raises questions about whether police caught the right person; key insiders in the case speak out for the first time on national television.

programme.title: Night of the Summer Solstice
programme.desc: When hikers find a 21-year-old UCLA student's body in a Los Angeles-area train tunnel, detectives wonder if Ron's interest in an alternative religion is connected to his murder.

programme.title: A Wanted Man
programme.desc: The question of a surgeon's whereabouts remains unanswered for five years after he disappears while on vacation in the Greek Islands with his wife, leaving behind financial ruin and mounting malpractice suits from patients in the U.S.

programme.title: The Life and Death of Princess Diana
programme.desc: New insights into the real story of the very private royal, including a look at Diana's troubled marriage, her turbulent life in the royal family and the investigation into her death.

programme.title: Jonestown: An American Tragedy
programme.desc: An in-depth look at the journalists who exposed the dangers of cult leader Reverend Jim Jones; interviews with witnesses to murders carried out by Jones' followers.

programme.title: Death of a Golden Girl
programme.desc: An aspiring Playboy model is brutally murdered in Miami after visiting a nightclub with her boyfriend.

programme.title: Over the Edge
programme.desc: Two decades after a woman falls to her death, police reopen the case and arrest her husband.

programme.title: Someone Was Watching
programme.desc: A mother, who seemed to be happily married, was found dead in her backyard spa.

programme.title: The Perfect Guy
programme.desc: A man steals millions of dollars by conning numerous women and businesses over 25 years; one woman brings together a group of his victims to hold him accountable and make him face justice.

programme.title: On a Dark, Deserted Highway
programme.desc: A deadly high-speed chase in Montana leads "Dateline" on a search through 50 years of history to unravel the mystery of how one man turned into a monster and committed one of the state's most notorious crimes.

programme.title: Mystery on the Mississippi
programme.desc: When a mother of four dies unexpectedly on Valentine's Day, her death is attributed to natural causes, but a detective suspects that someone murdered the woman.

programme.title: The Disappearance of Debbie Hawk

programme.title: Marine Mammals - Born to Swim
programme.desc: Every year some 15 million of us around the world cram onto little boats and head out onto the ocean, hoping for the encounter of a lifetime. For centuries whales and dolphins seem to have reached out to us, capturing our imaginations and our souls. Despite their popularity, much of their lives remain a mystery, taking place beneath the waves and beyond our reach.

programme.title: Cook Islands/ Kūki ''Airani
programme.desc: It's a miracle the first seafarers ever found the Cook Islands/ Kūki 'Airani scattered across two million square kilometres of the Pacific Ocean. But every year, these tropical islands become the destination for over three thousand Humpback whales who've undertaken one of the longest migrations on the planet. They come here to socialise, mate, and raise their young.

programme.title: The Power Of Plants - Race to Grow and Breed
programme.desc: Just like animals, the lives of plants are dominated by the need to become strong and pass on genes to the next generation - a race to grow and breed. They must race to beat their competition to the best light spots, and to make the most of perilously short seasons. And also like in the animal kingdom, different species have developed a near unending list of strategies to ensure their legacy is passed on.

programme.title: The Battle of the Horn/Kaziranga
programme.desc: Rhino horn is very expensive in the illegal market and the poachers know it. Kaziranga has the only concentrated population of the one horned Rhino in the world. And poachers are attracted to Kaziranga like ants are to sugar. The primary work of the forest department here is to then protect the rhino from the poachers and save the horn. We meet forest guard Shanti Ram Chetri who after 33 years of glorious service retires.

programme.title: Episode 002
programme.desc: Owls - with their huge eyes, flat faces and distinctive hoot - they are truly iconic!creatures. But how much do we really know about these mysterious nocturnal birds? We're about to find out as we follow the fate of new born baby owls as they grow up and learn to fly.

programme.title: Rumble in the Jungle
programme.desc: In this episode we explore why and how animals fight and reveal the ways in which they are programmed to survive at all costs. Most animals will defend themselves against predators, but many also do battle with members of the same species. Animals fight for two main reasons: for a mate or to defend their young or territory. And when animals fight, it can often be to the death.

programme.title: The reclaimed forest/Pakke
programme.desc: Hunting has been a long-standing cultural tradition in the North Eastern India for long. But with the shirking of the forests and endangering of the wildlife, hunting has become unsustainable. But it is not that this has stopped hunting. The architects of Pakke, a 800 sq Kms forest reserve, in the heart of the hunting villages has done a wonderful job of giving protection to the several endemic species here by keeping the forest safe from the hunters.

programme.title: Animals of Thanksgiving
programme.desc: Thanksgiving. A most treasured holiday, and not just in the USA; it continues to be celebrated across the world in many different guises. These traditions are all united by a celebration of the harvest and the generosity of the natural world. Many animals have weird and wonderful connections to the holidays. Turkeys are one of the most iconic characters, but deer, lobsters and even eagles are also part of the feast.

programme.title: American Mountains
programme.desc: Wildlife that inhabits mountainous regions has be able to survive successfully at high altitudes. Any creature that lives in the mountains must also be able to cope with changing temperatures. Many species of hoofed and herbivorous mammal such as GOATS, DEER, SHEEP AND LLAMAS have adapted well to living high in the mountains and are often found grazing on ledges and on cliff faces. These herbivores in turn attract large predators such as BEARS, COUGARS AND MOUNTAIN LIONS.

programme.title: Madagascar
programme.desc: Islands come in all shapes and sizes all over the world. Any land mass surrounded by water is an island. They are found in seas, oceans lakes and rivers. Atolls, Islets, keys or cays are formed either as result of land brea-king away, water encroaching on the land, or by volcanic eruptions on the sea bed . Islands are often isolated, which leads to the development of a unique flora, fauna and wildlife. The environmental eco-structure of islands differs widely, as does the wildlife.

programme.title: Amazon Rainforest
programme.desc: The Amazon. A magnificent broad-leafed rainforest. The heart of Brazil. The Amazon basin covers an impressive 7 million square kilometres. Rainforests are often known as the lungs of our planet. The Amazon Rainforest is the largest. Its value in terms of the Oxygen that it provides, and the Carbon Dioxide that it consumes is immeasurable. It is home to splendid, exquisite plant and animal species. The most diverse and numerous array of species found anywhere in the world.

programme.title: African Savannah
programme.desc: Grasslands cover nearly fifty percent of the African continent. African grasslands support vast and diverse wildlife. Due to the open and uncovered nature of grassland, predators are much easier to spot, giving smaller animals a chance to run away, hide and survive. Thanks to the lack of hiding places for predators, the African savannah regions support a much greater diversity of wildlife than temperate grasslands.

programme.title: The Hebrides: Land of Legends
programme.desc: Lying just off the coast of west Scotland, the Hebrides archipelago is made up of more than 500 islands and islets. Isolation from the mainland has made it the perfect breeding ground for millions of creatures, making it home to some of the largest gatherings, and greatest spectacles on the planet.

programme.title: The fear of the Stripes/Sunderbans
programme.desc: The Royal Bengal Tiger is in it's most primeval form here in the Sunderbans. `The tangled mangroves along the tributaries of the river Ganga are one of the most fearsome forests of the World. The tigers could kill humans and eat them. The people living around the forests are also one of the poorest in the country. They have to go inside the forest to eke out a living by catching crabs and fish. And that's the opportunity the tiger may seek.

programme.title: Wild Indochinas - Wild heart
programme.desc: Indochina; three ancient kingdoms, Laos, Vietnam and Cambodia, linked by one great river: the mighty Mekong. A mystical land shaped by the forces of the monsoon. A region ravaged by war but, like a Phoenix, risen from the ashes. Within its boundaries can be found one tenth of the world's species, and some of the richest ecosystems on the planet. This is the land of the Mother River, one of the most bio diverse regions on Earth.

programme.title: City of Dogs
programme.desc: Bred from wolves, Huskies have helped humans carve out an existence in Alaska's desolate wilderness. These dogs still maintain many physical adaptations of their wild ancestors, enabling them to withstand the fierce conditions of the Alaskan winter. And in Alaska's most extreme terrain, sled dogs are still the only form of transport. In the south, the modern city of Anchorage is still home to the start of the World's Toughest Race, a 1000 mile sled-dog race, known as the Iditarod.

programme.title: The Season's Feast
programme.desc: On the savannah of southern Africa, rains have turned the land green and lush. It's the time of plenty and for the cast of wild characters here, cashing in is priority number one. From polecat to aardwolf, some of the continent's most seldom seen creatures are out to make the most of the abundance. Some families gorge on the plentiful grasses, while for others there's no such thing as an easy meal, even at this time of year.

programme.title: Manatees on the Move
programme.desc: Manatees, sea cows, these gentle giants go by several names. They were once thought to be beautiful mermaids that could lure sailors to their deaths, though they probably won't win too many beauty contests. To retain their weight, manatees need to eat for 8 hours and consume 8% of their bodyweight every day. And keeping eating also means keeping moving - but though always on the move they're not exactly speedy.

programme.title: Seals - Clowns of the Sea
programme.desc: Much loved clowns of the sea, seals are endlessly fascinating. Even though they're not much more than bloated sausages on land, they're agile hunters and supremely graceful in the water. They en-tertain us with dramatic courtships, an endlessly playful sense of curiosity and some of the cutest babies on the planet.

programme.title: Snares/Tini Heke
programme.desc: Deep in the Southern Ocean, the Snares islands are one of the most pristine island wildernesses left on the planet. Every summer, millions of seabirds converge here to breed. More than 50,000 endemic Snares crested penguins battle massive Southern Ocean swells to come ashore. Deep in the forest they find their mates and raise their chicks in a frantic race to take advantage of the short subantarctic summer.

programme.title: Animal Record Breakers
programme.desc: We love to measure aspects of life at its extremes. The biggest, the tallest, heaviest, fastest, slowest - even the rarest. The creatures that hold the records for these categories are some of the most interesting in the natural world. Some are familiar and iconic, but it's also important to recognise some of the more surprising record breakers. These quirky and unusual animals that often go ignored are inventive, ingenious and awe-inspiring.

programme.title: Hunt or die
programme.desc: This episode explores nature's deadliest killers. From a tiny but deadly insect, to a pod of hungry Orca's, predators come in all sizes, and are found on every continent on earth. Chasing, stalking, ambushing or using camouflage, the way each predator hunts, catches and kills food is determined by many factors, including the anatomical adaptations of both the predator and the prey.

programme.title: Hidden UK
programme.desc: For its tiny size the UK is a hugely varied landscape with a surprising collection of remarkable and awe-inspiring wildlife.

programme.title: Downtown Porcupines
programme.desc: Anchorage is home to a huge number of wild porcupines, living in the city's parks, gardens and streets. Almost twice the average size, Anchorage's porcupines search for food here in the city, and find refuge during the bitter Alaskan winters. But life on the streets also takes its toll.Porcupines are the city's number one roadkill. In the wild, few animals other than wolves attempt to kill porcupines, and in the city, domesticated dogs can be as big a threat to the porcupines as wild wolves.

programme.title: Nature's Cutest
programme.desc: As we all know the natural world can be tough and challenging at times, but it can also be nothing short of adorable. Fluffy white seals, wobbly-kneed fawns, playing polar bear cubs, adorable teddy bear-like koalas - so much cute it would be impossible to decide which was the most adorable. But why do we consider some animals cute and others not? What it is about them that makes us fall in love? Perhaps it's those animals that remind us of ourselves?

programme.title: Destination Wild: Wild Madagascar
programme.desc: Millions of years ago, hundreds of castaway creatures crash-landed on Madagascar's rugged shores. Isolated from the mainland, evolution went into overdrive. Of almost a quarter of a million species found on the island are unique. This myriad of bizarre life forms had a huge impact on the early human settlers - one particular group of primates shaped their culture, fuelling folklore and legend that still guides their lives today. Limited Rights Available: Worldwide, Free TV Only

programme.title: The Choco
programme.desc: Spanning the western length of Colombia, the Chocó region is thought to be one of most biodiverse places on the planet. When the Andes Mountains rose around 60 million years ago they isolated this wild coast creating a haven for evolution. It is the wettest place on earth, on average 13m of water falls every year. Combined with the varied topography of the Western Andes and the year round tropical heat, it is the perfect environment for species to adapt and evolve.

programme.title: Born to be Wild
programme.desc: For every baby animal born, billions don't make it. Drought, flood, famine and predation; babies are born into a harsh world. The odds are so heavily stacked against some animals that it's a miracle any of their youngsters survive at-all. In this episode we discover the incredible lengths that nature's parents go to in order to ensure their progeny's survival.

programme.title: Serrania de le Macerena
programme.desc: In the middle of Colombia, lies an ancient, unique and little explored outcrop of sandstone; the Serrania de la Macarena. It forms part of the country's first ever national park - made up of lush jungle, shrubland and savannah, isolated peaks, winding rivers and spectacular waterfalls - where more than 15 million specimens were collected during early studies of the area. Called the 'treasure of the world', scientists believe it is a hugely important bank of biological diversity.

programme.title: May
programme.desc: While we celebrate may day, the coming of summer, there are many changes going on in the world. As snows finally melt in the mountains of Europe, chamois lambs have the chance to test out their climbing skills and explore their vertical home, watching all the time for eagles, their main predators. On the vast plains of the Russian the weird looking saiga antelope have their calves, while Florida enters its fire season and even the everglades can burn

programme.title: These Birds Are Made For Walking
programme.desc: Few things are more wondrous than the gift of flight, but some birds have chosen to give it up - the question is, why? Whether it's to save energy, tap into new food resources or invest in other skills, they all have their reasons. But one thing's for sure: it doesn't make flightless birds any less weird and wonderful. There are 60 species of bird that have given up the gift of flight, but they are not all related. Each have taken their own evolutionary path.

programme.title: Coasts - Rolling with the Waves
programme.desc: We love our coasts, and so do animals! The corridor of water where the open ocean transitions into coastal habitat is known as the surf zone. The churning forces of the waves clashing with the land make these some of the most food-rich waters on Earth. Nutrients are both washed off the coast from rain and rivers, but also pushed up from the depths thanks to waves and currents.

programme.title: Extinction! Going, going, gone!
programme.desc: Extinction, a daunting and confusing word. A force of nature, that sees the end of species, but also heralds the birth of others. Right now the extinction rate could be as much as 10,000 times faster than it should be. 20% of fish, a fifth of all reptiles and a quarter of mammals face extinction. If we are to do anything to stem the tide of extinction we must understand the lifestyles of those in danger.

programme.title: Caribbean
programme.desc: The Caribbean has been shaped by millions of years of unstoppable volcanic forces and ferocious hurricanes, creating a network of 7,000 islands, each one more unique than the next. From islets only a few miles long to landmasses with towering peaks, the habitats of this tropical paradise range from lush rainforests hiding untold species to multi-coloured coral reefs teeming with marine life.

programme.title: Deadly Bite
programme.desc: Many animals have evolved chemicals to enhance their chance of survival: some scorpions literally drug their potential mates, others use their poisons to defend or kill. The world of venoms and poisons, the apparatus designed to deliver the payload and the strategies that animals employ to use them most effectively is a rich and varied example of natural selection and evolution in action.

programme.title: The Great Barrier Reef
programme.desc: One of Australia's most remarkable natural gifts. The Great Barrier Reef in all it's breath-taking beauty. It is the world's largest coral reef, acknowledged as one of the seven wonders of the natural world, and viewed from a greater distance it's easy to understand why. It is larger than the Great Wall of China and the only living thing on earth visible from space. The Great Barrier Reef supports a vast array of life forms.

programme.title: Arctic
programme.desc: The Arctic is alive with a fascinating assortment of wildlife and species that are unique to this Polar environment. Most of are rarely or never seen outside the Arctic Circle. They live and thrive in a hostile environment of ice, polar desert, wind-swept open tundra, ancient glacial formations, sub zero sea temperatures and an incredible variety of geographical topo-graphy from open plain and valleys to mountainous peaks and deep water fiords.

programme.title: American Praire
programme.desc: Prairies are a temperate grassland. Vast great plains, extremely hot in summer and cold in winter. Moderate rainfall, and a composition of grasses, herbs and shrubs, rather than trees characterise these plains. Most of North America was a vast prairie before European settlement and agriculture radically altered the environment.

programme.title: Jungle of Asia
programme.desc: Some of the most beautiful rainforest, jungle landscape and wildlife are in Asia. The rainforests of Asia stretch from India and Burma in the west to Malaysia and the islands of Java and Borneo in the east. The Great teak forests and Jungles in Asia have long been under threat from intensive logging and industrial farming of cash crops. Slash and burn agriculture has also taken a heavy toll on the eco-structure and environment. Bangladesh has the largest mangrove forests in the world.

programme.title: Vancouver
programme.desc: Nestled alongside Canada's south west coast, Vancouver Island is home to the richest Pacific wildlife. Sea lions and killer whales are among the marine predators enjoying the abundant seafood in the surrounding waters, while black bears, marmots and beavers enjoy the rich pickings on land. But each fall, the islands inhabitants must adapt and prepare to face the coming winter. Some will leave, among them humpback whales and turkey vultures who migrate to warmer climes.

programme.title: A life for animals
programme.desc: Hannah runs a health check on two female cheetahs with veterinarian Maaike. She then goes into the wilderness with Naankuse founder Marlice. Together they go in search of the elephant Apollo, which was resettled in the sanctuary. The former "problem" elephant now leads a peaceful life here.

programme.title: Seasons Of The Otter
programme.desc: One of the most loves animals, famed for its playful nature and incredible underwater agility. Yet most of the life of the otter goes unseen. Following the first year in the life of a young otter family, we'll reveal the secrets of the otter's world. Otter life is often a challenge, and especially so for a young family trying to make it through winter. Two pups were born last spring, and as they approach their first birthdays the time with their mother is coming to its end.

programme.title: Moose Mayhem
programme.desc: This unique arctic city is home over 2000 moose! And these notorious animals are running riot... Crossing busy highways, giving birth in backyards, and even doing battle, right here in suburbia! But life on the streets is fraught with danger...and in this expanding city, more highways mean more moose deaths. But the people of Anchorage are on a mission, to protect the most iconic animal in this Wild City.

programme.title: Maui and Moloka''
programme.desc: In episode two we take a look at Maui and Moloka'i. In the middle of the archipelago they form the heart of Hawaii. The second largest island of Hawai'i - Maui - is a true paradise for surfers. Archie Kalepa was one of the first big wave surfers and is still chasing the thrill today. The ukulele represents the sound of the islands like no other instrument. Eric Devine has been building the plucked string instrument for 20 years. In Kula he goes in search of the perfect wood.

programme.title: Elephant 911/North Bengal
programme.desc: Elephant human conflict has been going on in India for decades. Only now it has increased because of the shrinking forests and the expanding human habitation. North Bengal with it's fragmented habitat of tea gardens, human habitation and paddy fields is a hot bed of conflict. We follow an elephant flying squad which is responsible for keeping the elephants away from these human dominated landscapes.

programme.title: Sexy Beasts
programme.desc: Driven by surging hormones, every creature on the planet, big or small, will do whatever it takes to find and secure a mate. For some this will take the fight of their lives, while others must preen, prance and party their way to success. From one night stands and group sex to lifelong love and unbreakable bonds, when it comes to finding a mate the animal kingdom has it all. The need to breed manifests itself in all sorts of wonderful antics, displays and behaviours.

programme.title: Life at the Extremes
programme.desc: In nature, competition for territory is so extreme that some animals have resorted to living in incredible hostile conditions. From brutal cold, to extreme heat, from the ocean depths, to the driest of deserts, this episode showcases some incredible survival stories in the world's most inhospitable environments.

programme.title: Egypt
programme.desc: 96% of Egypt's lands are sun-blistered desert. Rock and sand dominate this country, creating a beautiful but hostile environment. Yet it was home to the Worlds greatest ancient civilisation, which flourished for millennia and still captivates us today. These harsh lands also hold amazing animals that can survive and even thrive, able to cope with and profit from the searing temperatures and lack of moisture.

programme.title: Lion - Africa's Super Power
programme.desc: The endless plains of East Africa is a paradise for lions. The most social of all cats, lions form prides that are unlike any other animals. Together, they'll hunt, raise their young and defend their territory. With such a close family and plentiful home, the pride welcomes new babies every year. But new children introduces new dangers.

programme.title: Meet the Marsupials
programme.desc: Few countries have a more iconic representative in the animal kingdom than Australia and the marsupial. Once marsupials were found across the planet, but over time they found their way to the outback, leaving Australia as an ark carrying the future of pouch mammals. As varied as they are unusual, marsupials are a weird and wonderful mob of animals who carry their young in a pouch.

programme.title: Falklands
programme.desc: The Falkland Islands' pristine coastlines and bountiful seas offer a lifeline and breeding centre for millions of penguins each year. Though while some find sanctuary on dry land, there's a daily battle to survive in the waters which surround these wild and rocky shores.

programme.title: Return of the Sharks
programme.desc: In the aftermath of Cape Towns biggest storm in 2 decades, there's a whole lot of work to be done at the Two Oceans Aquarium! The pressure builds as nine Ragged-Toothed Sharks are on their way from East London for their introduction to the new, highly anticipated predator exhibit. Join the team in one last push to complete the giant tank in time for its incoming residents and see the experience the culmination of a year of hard work coming together, at the Two Oceans Aquarium!

programme.title: Animals of the Bible
programme.desc: The bible is one of the most famous texts on earth. But it doesn't just concern humans, it also mentions animals - and some of these are probably not what you'd expect. We've all heard of the ox and the ass, the donkey that carried Mary, but did you know gazelles are mentioned in the bible? Or that great whales, cunning leopards and even the energetic hyrax feature?

programme.title: Bears Behaving Badly
programme.desc: Anchorage is home to hundreds of black bears. And it's these black bears, that are patrolling the city. With their brains, their brawn and their cunning, these bears have mastered life in this urban jungle. When Spring arrives the bears hit the city as it's time to start eating. And these bears have found a source of food that is much easier to catch than a slippery salmon - it's trash. And it is everywhere. The city's bins and dumpsters have become the perfect bear restaurant.

programme.title: The Green Corridors
programme.desc: The tropical rainforests of Costa Rica provide an invaluable habitat to several emblematic species, such as jaguars, tapirs, white-lipped peccaries, spider monkeys, the very rear green macaw, amongst many others. Most of them are protected in national parks, reserves and wildlife refuges. However, the long-term survival of these ecosystems and of their biodiversity rely on the success of connecting wildlife populations throughout the country.

programme.title: Migrations - Herds on the Move
programme.desc: Whether driven by the search for food or the simple will to survive, great herd migrations are some of the most spectacular events of the natural world.

programme.title: Longevity
programme.desc: Aldabra Tortoise, Matriarch Elephants, Kittiwakes, Honey Bees, Hydra, Lions In this episode of Aging in the Wild, we explore the physiological secrets and factors that determine life expectancy in various animal species. From the seventy-year-old elephant to the quasi-immortal hydra, and the more than a hundred-year-old tortoise, we explore life expectancy, longevity and senescence. Can we distinguish between the effects of the environment and the internal adaptations that lead to longevity?

programme.title: Power & Dominance
programme.desc: Bighorn Sheep, Elk, Male Elephants, Marmots, Baboons, Rhinos Observing two massive elk clashing their antlers is to witness a true demonstration of power. For other species, such as the European marmot, remaining in power is a matter of collaborating with family and community. Are these animals forced to give up their hard-won social status as they age? Through this lens, we take a deep and entertaining look at the challenges faced by those in power ... and what it takes to stay there.

programme.title: The Play's The Thing

programme.title: The Ides Of March

programme.title: Chakram
programme.desc: Xena (Lucy Lawless) has no recollection of being a warrior after she and Gabrielle (Renee O'Connor) are resurrected from the dead by Eli (Tim Omundson).

programme.title: Succession
programme.desc: Ares (Kevin Smith) merges Xena (Lucy Lawless) and Gabrielle (Renee O'Connor) into the same body and forces them to fight Mavican (Jenya Lano), Ares' potential right hand.

programme.title: Animal Attraction
programme.desc: Xena (Lucy Lawless), Gabrielle (Renee O'Connor), Joxer (Ted Raimi) and Amarice (Jennifer Sky) travel to the town of Spamona, where Xena is shocked to learn that she is pregnant.

programme.title: Them Bones, Them Bones
programme.desc: The spirit of the evil Shamaness Alti (Claire Stansfield) attempts to capture the soul of Xena's (Lucy Lawless) unborn child.

programme.title: Purity
programme.desc: When Xena (Lucy Lawless) returns to Chin to recover Lao Ma's book of power, she must defeat one of Lao Ma's twin daughters, who wants to acquire the power for her own evil purposes.

programme.title: Back in the Bottle
programme.desc: Xena (Lucy Lawless) must master Lao Ma's powers to save Gabrielle (Renee O'Connor), Joxer (Ted Raimi), and the people of Chin from a militia led by the evil spirits of Pao Ssu (Marie Matiko) and her brother, Ming Tien (Daniel Sing).

programme.title: Little Problems
programme.desc: Gabrielle (Renee O'Connor) and Aphrodite (Alexandra Tydings) have until sundown to save Xena's (Lucy Lawless) soul from being trapped inside a young girl forever.

programme.title: Seeds of Faith
programme.desc: Eli (Timothy Omundson) tries to overthrow the gods by battling Ares (Kevin Smith); Xena (Lucy Lawless) learns the identity of her baby's father.

programme.title: Lyre, Lyre, Hearts On Fire
programme.desc: A musical episode in which Xena (Lucy Lawless) is reunited with her mother, Cyrene (Darien Takle), Joxer (Ted Raimi) is reunited with his twin and Gabrielle (Renee O'Connor) meets Draco (Jay Laga'aia).

programme.title: Punch Lines
programme.desc: Gabrielle (Renee O'Connor) and Argo are shrunken into miniature versions of themselves when they cross paths with Lachrymose (Jon Gadsby), the god of despair.

programme.title: God Fearing Child
programme.desc: Elliott and Maya (Enrico Colantoni, Laura San Giacomo) decide to keep their newfound relationship a secret. With George Segal.

programme.title: Eternal Bonds
programme.desc: While Xena (Lucy Lawless) fights off priests' armies, Gabrielle (Renee O'Connor) seeks an antidote for Joxer's (Ted Raimi) poisonous wound.

programme.title: Amphipolis Under Siege
programme.desc: Xena's (Lucy Lawless) hometown, Amphipolis, is attacked by Athena's (Paris Jefferson) warriors in an attempt to get Xena's child.

programme.title: Married With Fishsticks
programme.desc: A merman (Ted Raimi) convinces an injured Gabrielle (Renee O'Connor) that she is his wife and the mother of his children.

programme.title: Lifeblood
programme.desc: Xena and Gabrielle (Lucy Lawless, Renee O'Connor) must prevent an Amazon war against the Samite nomads.

programme.desc: Joxer (Ted Raimi) breaks Amazon laws that force Queen Gabrielle (Renée O'Connor) to choose between settling down in the Amazon village and life on the road with Xena (Lucy Lawless).

programme.title: Antony & Cleopatra
programme.desc: When Cleopatra (Josephine Davison) is murdered, Xena (Lucy Lawless) assumes her identity to uncover the assassin and protect Egypt.

programme.title: Looking Death in the Eye
programme.desc: Joxer (Ted Raimi), now in his 60s, finds the last scroll written by Gabrielle (Renee O'Connor), recounting their battle to protect Xena's (Lucy Lawless) child.

programme.title: Livia
programme.desc: Xena and Gabrielle (Lucy Lawless, Renee O'Connor) are freed from their icy prison after 25 years and set out to find Eve (Adrienne Wilkinson), who has become a fearless commander in Rome.

programme.title: Eve
programme.desc: Eve (Adrienne Wilkinson) continues her quest to kill all of Eli's cult followers, and Xena (Lucy Lawless) must decide how to stop her.

programme.title: Motherhood
programme.desc: Xena (Lucy Lawless) battles the gods with her newfound power as Eve (Adrienne Wilkinson) atones for her past sins.

programme.title: Coming Home
programme.desc: Ares (Kevin Smith) needs Xena's (Lucy Lawless) help to restore his godly powers, but he gets more than he bargained for when the Furies play a trick on him. With Renee O'Connor and Sela Apera.

programme.title: Haunting of Amphipolis
programme.desc: On her trip home, Xena (Lucy Lawless) finds the town possessed and sinister powers awaiting her. With Renee O'Connor, Charles Mesure and Adrienne Wilkinson.

programme.title: Heart of Darkness
programme.desc: Xena (Lucy Lawless) must devise a plan to avoid inheriting the kingdom of hell. With Renee O'Connor.

programme.title: Who's Gurkham?
programme.desc: Gabrielle (Renee O'Connor) sets out on a rescue mission to North Africa with the gang in tow when she discovers her niece has been kidnapped. With Lucy Lawless, Adrienne Wilkinson, William Gregory Lee and Calvin Tuteao.

programme.title: Legacy
programme.desc: Xena and Gabrielle (Lucy Lawless, Renee O'Connor) try to help two warring African tribes unite against their Roman enemies.

programme.title: The Abyss
programme.desc: Xena and Gabrielle (Lucy Lawless, Renee O'Connor) are confronted by cannibals as they search for Virgil (William Gregory Lee).

programme.title: The Rheingold
programme.desc: Beowulf (guest star Renato Bartolomei), a Norse warrior, sets out on a quest with Xena (Lucy Lawless) after she decides to right a wrong from her dark past.

programme.title: The Ring
programme.desc: Xena (Lucy Lawless) must battle Grindl, a monster she created when she was an evil warrior, in order to recover a dangerous enchanted ring. With Renee O'Connor, Glen Levy, Luanne Gordon, Brittney Powell and Renato Bartolomei.

programme.title: Return of the Valkyrie
programme.desc: Xena (Lucy Lawless) has amnesia as Hrothgar's (guest star John Leigh) bride, Wealthea, and must regain her memory in order to save Gabrielle (Renee O'Connor).

programme.title: Old Ares Had A Farm
programme.desc: Xena (Lucy Lawless) disguises Ares (Kevin Smith) as a farmer to hide him from warlords seeking revenge.

programme.title: Dangerous Prey
programme.desc: Xena (Lucy Lawless) becomes the ultimate prey for a deranged Amazon hunter, Prince Morloch (guest star Sandy Winton).

programme.title: The God You Know
programme.desc: Michael the archangel (guest star Charles Mesure) orders Xena (Lucy Lawless) to hunt down the Roman emperor Caligula (guest star Alexis Arquette), who has become immortal, and kill him.

programme.title: You Are There
programme.desc: A tabloid reporter (guest star Michael Hurst) tries to get the scoop on Xena (Lucy Lawless) and her motivation for her quest to obtain the legendary golden apples from Valhalla. With Renee O'Connor.

programme.title: Path of Vengeance
programme.desc: Eve (Adrienne Wilkinson) faces execution when she returns to Amazon lands to make amends for the past. With Lucy Lawless and Renee O'Connor.

programme.title: To Helicon And Back
programme.desc: Gabrielle (Renee O'Connor) leads the Amazons to Helicon to rescue kidnapped Queen Varia (guest star Tsianina Joelson). With Lucy Lawless.

programme.title: Send in the Clones
programme.desc: Three modern-day fans of Xena create clones of Xena and Gabrielle (Lucy Lawless, Renee O'Connor).

programme.title: Last of the Centaurs
programme.desc: Xena (Lucy Lawless) and Gabrielle (Renee O'Connor) must save a young centaur from the clutches of Lord Belach (Marton Csokas).

programme.title: Family Feud
programme.desc: Steve Harvey assumes the hosting duties for this daytime game show in which five members of one family are pitted against five members of another family. Each team's goal is to guess the results of audience survey questions. A player from each team initially faces off, answering the question to earn the chance to either pass or play. The winning family gets a chance to earn extra cash in a bonus round.

Each team's goal is to guess the results of audience survey questions. A player from each team initially faces off, answering the question to earn the chance to either pass or play. The winning family gets a chance to earn extra cash in a bonus round.

programme.title: Measure It
programme.desc: How distance, time, speed, weight and temperature are measured; weighing a whale; how a speedometer works; the National Institute of Standards and Technology; measuring tapes made by Stanley Tools.

programme.title: Harvesting
programme.desc: Cutting, digging, picking, stripping, shaking, and raking--whatever the crop, there's a custom machine to harvest it; it all began with handpicking, and today it's often one man and one machine harvesting hundreds of acres in a single day.
